quoted_clause: "[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] — model-service latency p99 degrades past the 800 ms SLO under concurrent load; downstream network jitter p99 = 120 ms (scenario inputs to be measured)."
observed: The 120 ms downstream-jitter figure is introduced as a scenario input and then never used: it does not appear in any budget, threshold, trip condition, or derived quantity in the chapter. A reader cannot tell whether the breaker's 5-timeout trip threshold is sensitive to it, or whether it is a leftover from an earlier draft.
evidence: Grep of the chunk: "120 ms" occurs once, in this sentence. The breaker's mechanism is "trip after 5 consecutive timeouts" and its FACT set is "timeout count / 30s; fallback activation rate; recovery grace-period latency" — none of which references the jitter distribution.
root_cause: An input was added to make the scenario feel complete without being wired into the mechanism it is supposed to inform.
correction: Either use it — e.g. state that the 5-timeout trip threshold is chosen relative to the 120 ms jitter p99 (a timeout budget of X ms is ~N× the jitter p99, so a single jitter spike does not trip the breaker) — or delete it. If retained, it should appear in the breaker FACT set as a measured quantity (e.g. downstream timeout rate) and in Table 26-1.
acceptance_test: Every scenario input introduced in §3 appears in at least one budget, threshold, or FACT set; no input is introduced and abandoned.

quoted_clause: "How does fleet-wide model versioning interact with per-shard caching, and what FACTs govern safe rollouts?"
observed: "Per-shard caching" is not a term used anywhere else in the chapter or in the patterns library. The chapter's caching concepts are the semantic response cache (Pattern B), prefix caching (referenced in §2.1), and prompt caching. The open question therefore names a mechanism the reader has not been introduced to, which is exactly the failure mode the chapter's own §7 preamble tries to avoid ("each becomes a testable HYPOTHESIS once its FACT instrumentation and pass criterion are specified").
evidence: Table 26-3's caching entry is "Semantic Response Cache"; §2.1's matrix mentions "prefix caching"; no "per-shard cache" concept is defined in the chunk.
root_cause: The open question was drafted against a different vocabulary than the chapter settled on.
correction: Rewrite the question in the chapter's own terms — e.g. "How does fleet-wide model versioning interact with the semantic response cache and with prefix caching, and what FACTs govern safe rollouts (cache-key revision, corpus snapshot, model revision)?" — and make sure the named mechanisms exist in the chapter.
acceptance_test: Every mechanism named in §7 is defined earlier in the book; no term in §7 is unique to §7.

quoted_clause: "**Rule key (R-codes).** The pattern templates cite the book's standing rules by code; the codes and their text: **R-01** ... **R-03** ... **R-04** ... **R-05** ... **R-07** ... **R-10** ... **R-13** ..."
observed: The list is presented as "the codes and their text" but is non-contiguous (R-02, R-06, R-08, R-09, R-11, R-12 are absent), and no pointer tells the reader where the full rule set lives. A reader who wants to know whether R-06 exists, or what R-02 says, has nowhere to go.
evidence: The chapter cites seven codes spanning R-01 to R-13 with six gaps; the phrase "the codes and their text" implies completeness.
root_cause: The list was assembled from the codes this chapter happens to cite, but written as if it were the complete key.
correction: Either (a) retitle as "the rules cited in this chapter" and add a pointer to the book's full rule key (chapter and section), or (b) reproduce the complete key. Also add the pointer so the codes are navigable.
acceptance_test: The R-code list states whether it is complete and gives a resolvable pointer to the full set; every R-code cited in Ch 26 appears in that list.

quoted_clause: "**Quantization decision record.** The architecture decision record names the active constraint, affected tensors, and proposed deployment configuration. ... [ILLUSTRATIVE] conceptual"
observed: This paragraph is a self-contained treatment of the quantization ADR (it names three chapters and an acceptance-condition set) but sits inside §2.1, whose declared subject is the workload-to-strategy decision matrix, with no subheading of its own. It interrupts the matrix's argument and is invisible to anyone scanning headings.
evidence: §2.1's opening: "The matrix below is the first-pass mapping from a new workload's dominant constraint to the strategy class worth evaluating first". The quantization paragraph follows the matrix and the Fig 26.1 provenance note with no heading, and its content (ADR structure, resource ledger, acceptance conditions) is unrelated to the matrix.
root_cause: A separate topic was appended to the matrix section rather than given its own heading or its own place in the chapter.
correction: Give it a numbered subheading (e.g. "2.2 Quantization decision record") or move it to the chapter's measurement section, where the ADR/acceptance-condition material sits naturally next to Table 26-1. If it stays in §2.1, add a one-line transition explaining why the quantization ADR belongs in the workload-to-strategy discussion.
acceptance_test: Every paragraph in §2.1 either belongs to the matrix discussion or sits under its own subheading; the chapter's heading structure exposes the quantization material to a scanning reader.

quoted_clause: "Dashboards surface FACT trends; alerts fire when DERIVED quantities cross safety boundaries (e.g., the p99 TTFT SLO, the fallback-rate FACT target < 10% of Table 26-2, or the queue-depth limits of Ch 15)."
observed: The three examples given are not DERIVED quantities: p99 TTFT is a measured FACT (as §2 itself lists it: "query latency p99"), the fallback rate is a FACT, and queue depth is a FACT. The sentence's own first clause ("Dashboards surface FACT trends") already assigns these to the FACT side, so the paragraph contradicts itself.
evidence: §2: "FACT — a verified runtime quantity (e.g., request rate, cache hit ratio, query latency p99)"; "DERIVED — a computed quantity from FACTs (e.g., throughput per shard, cost per query, fleet-wide rps)". Table 26-1's FACT columns are exactly p99 latency, hit ratio, timeout count, SM utilization.
root_cause: The alert list was written as a list of thresholds without checking each item's status, and the FACT/DERIVED distinction was applied to the sentence rather than to the items.
correction: Rewrite the sentence to separate the two: dashboards surface FACT trends (p99 TTFT, hit ratio, shed rate, queue depth, SM utilization); alerts fire when a FACT crosses a threshold OR when a DERIVED quantity (throughput per shard, cost per query, fleet-wide rps, SLO compliance) crosses a boundary. Use the chapter's own DERIVED examples so the distinction is demonstrated rather than asserted.
acceptance_test: Every item in §4's alert list is correctly classified as FACT or DERIVED, and the list contains at least one item of each kind.

quoted_clause: "sharding distributes the model across the node so decode lands in the bandwidth-bound regime (the low-batch regime of Ch. 8; batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware decide whether it stays there)"
observed: Causal misattribution: sharding (tensor parallelism) does not cause decode to be bandwidth-bound. Decode is bandwidth-bound because the per-step work is dominated by reading the weights and the KV cache at low batch — a property of the arithmetic intensity of the decode step, not of how the model is partitioned. The parenthetical correctly qualifies the regime but the main clause asserts a false causal link.
evidence: §3 Pattern A states the same regime correctly: "decode latency is bandwidth-bound in the low-batch decode regime of Ch. 8 ... whether decode binds on bandwidth or compute depends on batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware" — with no causal role for TP. TP's role is stated separately: "per-token throughput is governed by the node's aggregate HBM bandwidth and approaches 8× the single-GPU rate only to the extent tensor-parallel communication and other overheads are negligible".
root_cause: Two independent facts (TP placement; low-batch decode regime) were compressed into one causal sentence.
correction: Rewrite as: "sharding distributes the model across the node's GPUs so the aggregate HBM bandwidth available to a decode step is 8× a single GPU's; at the low batch sizes of this scenario, decode is bandwidth-bound (Ch 8), so that aggregate bandwidth is what governs per-token latency." This also makes the TP→bandwidth link explicit rather than implied.
acceptance_test: No sentence in Ch 26 asserts that sharding or tensor parallelism causes a compute/bandwidth regime; the regime is attributed to batch size, precision, kernel and hardware, and TP is attributed to aggregate bandwidth and communication overhead.

quoted_clause: "| Fine-tuning | N/A | N/A | Memory + interconnect | Precision-aware optimizer (LoRA/QLoRA) before full FT; gradient checkpointing (Ch 7) |"
observed: The pointer for gradient checkpointing is Ch 7, which this chapter uses for KV/quantization memory accounting (Ch 7, 22 for KV bytes/token; Ch 7 for the representation and memory accounting of quantization). Gradient checkpointing is a training-time activation-memory technique; the chapter's own Training row points to Ch 10 for parallelism. The pointer is likely wrong.
evidence: §2.1's own quantization paragraph: "Chapter 7 establishes the representation and memory accounting". §2.1's Training row: "Parallelism split (DP/TP/PP/FSDP) sized to model and cluster (Ch 10)". Gradient checkpointing appears in neither.
root_cause: The row's pointer was filled with the chapter that covers "memory" rather than the chapter that covers training.
correction: Verify where gradient checkpointing is treated in the book and point there (likely Ch 10, or a training chapter if one exists); if it is not treated anywhere, either add a short treatment or replace the pointer with a chapter that does cover the technique.
acceptance_test: Every technique named in the §2.1 matrix is treated in the chapter it points to; a reader following the Fine-tuning row's pointer finds gradient checkpointing discussed.

quoted_clause: "The architect instruments all three scenario quantities, observes the derived quantities in real time, and validates each HYPOTHESIS against measured traffic. The result: one 8×H100 serving host + a 35% semantic response cache + circuit breaker yields an illustrative p99 TTFT ≈ 250 ms versus the ~450 ms uncached single-node baseline ... (scenario outcome, not a measured benchmark)."
observed: The paragraph narrates a completed measurement activity ("instruments ... in real time, and validates each HYPOTHESIS against measured traffic") that the chapter explicitly says did not happen: §8 Step 1 states "no author-run load test produced them", and §8 Step 3 states the 285 ms figure is "illustrative values to show how a hypothesis is tested, not a real experiment the book ran". The parenthetical "(scenario outcome, not a measured benchmark)" partially retracts the narration but does not fix it.
evidence: §8 Step 1: "These are assumed baseline inputs, not gathered FACTs (R-07): no author-run load test produced them, so they are labeled an assumed baseline for a worked example (an input to the math), not a measured runtime quantity a FACT would be." §8 Step 3: "in this scenario these are illustrative values to show how a hypothesis is tested, not a real experiment the book ran."
root_cause: The capstone was written in the voice of a completed engagement and then annotated with disclaimers rather than rewritten in the voice of a worked example.
correction: Rewrite the paragraph in the indicative-of-a-template voice: "In a real engagement the architect would instrument ..., observe ..., and validate ... . The worked example below carries that loop with assumed inputs; the resulting configuration is recorded as Table 26-2 (scenario outcome, not a measured benchmark)." Keep the disclaimers but stop narrating an activity that did not occur.
acceptance_test: No paragraph in Ch 26 narrates a measurement, deployment or validation as having occurred unless the chapter states that it did; the tense of the capstone narrative matches the chapter's evidence labels.

quoted_clause: "The offered rate stays flat at 1.5× users because it is a declared scenario input capped at the host's ~2.0 rps sustainable ceiling (the Scenario above), not a per-user rate."
observed: The sentence is garbled: "stays flat at 1.5× users" states the opposite of what is meant (the rate stays flat while the user count grows 1.5×). The reader has to reconstruct the intended meaning from the following sentences.
evidence: The next two sentences make the intent clear: "The user count does not raise what one host sustains: holding ~2.0 rps while the concurrent population grows from ~100 to ~150 implies a ~33% lower per-concurrent-user rate." (Check: 2.0/100 = 0.020 rps per concurrent user; 2.0/150 = 0.0133; ratio 0.667 → 33% lower ✓.)
root_cause: Compressed rewrite of a longer explanation.
correction: Rewrite as: "The offered rate stays flat at ~2.0 rps while the user count grows 1.5×, because the rate is a declared scenario input capped at the host's ~2.0 rps sustainable ceiling (see the Scenario above) rather than a per-user rate."
acceptance_test: The sentence parses on first reading and states which quantity is flat and which grows.

quoted_clause: "The reproducible two-point model that yields these numbers is `render/capstone_calc.py`; a real deployment must measure the actual cache-hit latency distribution (not a point mass), the prefill queue at 1.3 rps, and the per-query cost"
observed: A repository-relative path is given as the reproducibility reference. A reader holding the book cannot resolve `render/capstone_calc.py` without knowing the repository layout; the book elsewhere (per the chapter's own reproducibility conventions) should point to a resolvable location (URL plus version/commit) for the artifact.
evidence: The path is given with no URL, no repository name, no commit or version, and no pointer to the book's reproducibility appendix.
root_cause: An internal development path was substituted for a published artifact reference.
correction: Give the artifact's resolvable location (repository URL + path + commit/release tag) and cross-reference the book's reproducibility appendix, consistent with how other first-party artifacts are cited in the book.
acceptance_test: Every artifact path printed in the book resolves for a reader who has only the book; the path is accompanied by a version identifier.

quoted_clause: "The Solution Architect's Toolkit answers two concerns — scalability and reliability — and is organized as pattern templates plus measurement rather than as three separate taxonomies"
observed: The stated scope ("two concerns — scalability and reliability") does not match the chapter's own catalogue, two of whose five patterns are about quality and cost (fine-tuning: "quality delta vs RAG"; RAG model selection: "cost/token", "retrieve-vs-generate surface"), and whose measurement section is explicitly about cost ("Measure cost per query as a first-class derived quantity"). The sentence also reads as a rebuttal to a prior review rather than as a description of the chapter.
evidence: Table 26-3's Minimal FACT sets include "quality delta vs RAG" and "cost/token"; §5 Mistake 3 is entirely about cost; §3's Capstone Execution is largely about cost bases.
root_cause: The scope sentence was narrowed to answer a framing objection and never re-opened against the chapter's actual content.
correction: Restate the scope to match the content — e.g. "The toolkit answers three concerns — scale, reliability, and cost/quality trade-offs — and is organised as pattern templates plus measurement" — and drop the "rather than as three separate taxonomies" clause, which references an alternative structure the reader never saw.
acceptance_test: The stated scope of the toolkit covers every concern addressed by the five patterns and by §4–§6; no sentence in §2 defends against a structure the book does not present.

The 'A.' prefix on the pointers also does not match the printed heading labels, so the pointers are doubly non-resolving.

Then grep the whole manuscript for 'A\.[0-9]' to catch any pointer outside this chunk. Consider adopting a single explicit label form (e.g. 'A §8' or 'App. A §8') and using it consistently, since the current 'A.10' form implies a numbering that does not exist.

Option (b) also resolves APPA-03 and APPA-04 below.

The appendix's own text also contains the sentence 'Fig 8.3 shows the data path.' immediately followed by the parenthetical '*(Fig 8.3 in Ch 8 shows the data path.)*', which is a duplicated statement within two sentences.

If Ch 8 §6 carries the same derivation, keep the full derivation in Ch 8 §6 (where Fig 8.3 lives) and reduce the appendix subsection to a two-sentence pointer with the headline numbers, or vice versa — but not both. Delete the redundant parenthetical '*(Fig 8.3 in Ch 8 shows the data path.)*'.

page_hint: Appendix A §7A (whole section) vs. post-snapshot note 'Diffusion language generation — 2026-10-28'
chapter: Appendix A §7A / Appendix A post-snapshot notes
quoted_clause: ## 7A. Alternative inference in detail (moved from Ch 3) ... Public artifacts now support more than one diffusion-language deployment pattern. LLaDA and Dream provide open checkpoints and generation code for masked/refinement-based language generation.
observed: Two substantial treatments of diffusion language generation appear inside the same appendix: §7A ('From corruption to learned generation', 'A language-generation trajectory', 'State reuse follows dependency boundaries') and the post-snapshot note 'Diffusion language generation — 2026-10-28'. Both cover LLaDA, DiffusionGemma, block editing, and the SGLang Gemma4Renoise path; §7A adds MDLM, flow matching, Fast-dLLM/dKV-Cache, Block Diffusion, DFlash. The overlap is not merely topical — the same artifacts are characterized twice, once as durable mechanism and once as a dated release catalog. Separately, §7A is durable (paper-by-paper) mechanism material sitting inside an appendix whose own framing is 'a dated field guide, not an evergreen ranking' and whose stated scope is the four 2026 families.
evidence: Both passages are in this chunk. §7A's own closing sentence (APPA-02) states the section was designed to sit in the model-understanding chapter, confirming it is not frontier-snapshot material.

Preferred: keep the durable paper-by-paper treatment in Ch 3 (where §7A's own rationale and Ch 3 §1's scope note point) and reduce the appendix's post-snapshot diffusion note to a short, dated pointer listing only what changed after 2026-08-30 (release dates, engine restrictions), with a cross-reference to Ch 3. If §7A stays in the appendix, then the post-snapshot diffusion note must be cut to the delta only, and the appendix's scope statement must be widened to say it also collects durable background.
acceptance_test: Each diffusion artifact (LLaDA, DiffusionGemma, MDLM, Block Diffusion, DFlash, dKV-Cache) is characterized once in the book; the appendix's scope statement matches what the appendix actually contains.

page_hint: Appendix A, 'The four families at a glance' → Fig A.1 definition paragraph vs. the italic sparsity paragraph
quoted_clause: 'active' ... means the parameters that participate in the forward pass for a given token: the routed experts dispatched for that token, the shared/always-on experts, and the attention and embedding/head parameters that run for every token. ... Qwen's N-gram embedding table is excluded from the active-fraction denominator below — see the Fig A.1 note ... the separate 51 B n-gram embedding and 4 B MTP modules are excluded from both numerator and denominator, so this is a *backbone* fraction
observed: Two adjacent statements disagree about the Qwen numerator. The definition paragraph says the n-gram embedding table is excluded from the denominator only; the italic paragraph says the 51 B n-gram embedding is excluded from both numerator and denominator. The distinction is material: under the appendix's own definition (embedding parameters that run for every token count as active), including the 51 B n-gram table in the numerator would give 57 B / 125 B ≈ 45.6% rather than 4.8% — a factor of ~9.5 in the headline number. The appendix also states elsewhere (§3) that the n-gram tables are 'held off the accelerator and prefetched from host memory', i.e. they do participate in the forward pass, which is precisely the case the definition paragraph says counts as active.
evidence: Both quoted clauses are in this chunk; 6/125 = 4.8% and 57/125 = 45.6% are the two readings. The Fig A.1 caption itself says 'the Qwen bar is its 125 B backbone only', consistent with the 'both numerator and denominator' reading, so the definition paragraph is the outlier.
root_cause: The 'active' definition was written for the general case and then applied to Qwen's unusual split (backbone + separately offloaded n-gram table) without amending the definition to carve out the exception; the two statements were never reconciled.
correction: Amend the definition paragraph to state the exception explicitly and consistently: the numerator excludes the separately offloaded n-gram embedding table and the MTP module for Qwen only, and the resulting figure is a backbone-only ratio, not a fraction of the deployed parameter inventory. Alternatively, report both (4.8% backbone-only and 45.6% including the n-gram table) so the reader can see how much of the 'extreme sparsity' signal is an artifact of the denominator choice. Also state in the definition that 'active' is not a proxy for per-token FLOPs (already stated as clause (b)) — the Qwen case is a live example of why.
acceptance_test: The definition paragraph and the sparsity paragraph agree on whether the 51 B n-gram table is in the numerator; a reader can compute 4.8% from the stated inputs without ambiguity.

page_hint: Appendix A, 'Post-snapshot technology notes — 2026-10-28' editorial note vs. the four notes that follow
quoted_clause: A note keeps its place in Appendix A only when it changes how that comparison or the canonical arithmetic is read: a served-name or service-status change to a compared model, a new attention, KV or quantization mechanism that the chapters cite, or a correction to a source already listed. A note that only catalogs versions, pipelines or vendor backends, with no chapter cross-reference, belongs in a companion addendum rather than here.
observed: The appendix states an admission rule for its own post-snapshot notes and then breaks it in three of the four notes that follow. (i) 'Diffusion language generation — 2026-10-28' is a catalog of releases and engine restrictions (LLaDA, Dream, DiffusionGemma, Mercury 3, Gemini Diffusion, SGLang Gemma4Renoise) with no chapter cross-reference. (ii) 'Video systems snapshot — 2026-10-28' is a five-row table of video models and their mechanisms with no chapter cross-reference except one parenthetical pointing at Ch 8 §6. (iii) 'Intel backend supplement — 2026-10-28' is explicitly 'release identities, not one validated combined environment' and carries no chapter cross-reference at all. Only the quantization note and the DeepSeek service-status note satisfy the rule. The appendix thus spends roughly a third of its length on material its own editorial policy says belongs elsewhere.
evidence: The editorial note and the four notes are all in this chunk; the absence of chapter cross-references in the diffusion, video and Intel notes is directly observable.
root_cause: The editorial rule was written after the notes were drafted (or the notes were added without applying it), and no pass reconciled the notes against the rule.
correction: Apply the rule as written: move the diffusion, video and Intel notes to a companion addendum (or a separate dated appendix), keeping in Appendix A only the DeepSeek service-status note, the quantization-implementation note (which does cite mechanisms the chapters use), and any note that changes how the four-family comparison or the canonical arithmetic reads. If the notes are to stay, amend the editorial rule to admit them and add the missing chapter cross-references — but then the rule must state what a note may contain, not only what it must change.
acceptance_test: Every retained post-snapshot note either (a) changes how the four-family comparison or the canonical arithmetic is read, or (b) carries an explicit chapter cross-reference; the editorial rule and the notes are consistent.

page_hint: Appendix A §7A, 'Deriving attention FLOPs for a whole-clip video workload', final paragraph
quoted_clause: 'Five-second clip,' '121 frames,' and '27,280 latent tokens' describe related but different quantities.
observed: Terminology slip: 27,280 is the count of transformer patch positions (N = T_l × H_l/2 × W_l/2 = 31 × 22 × 40), not latent tokens. The latent spatial-temporal cell count is 109,120, and the appendix states this correctly two paragraphs earlier ('There are 109,120 latent spatial-temporal cells, each with 48 channels. Patching reduces the number of transformer positions'). Calling the post-patch count 'latent tokens' contradicts the appendix's own careful distinction between latent cells and transformer positions, and the same section elsewhere says 'all 27,280 tokens'.
evidence: Both statements are in this chunk; N = 31 × 22 × 40 = 27,280 and cells = 31 × 44 × 80 = 109,120.
root_cause: Loose reuse of 'latent' as a synonym for 'video-derived' in a passage whose point is that these quantities are different.
correction: Replace '27,280 latent tokens' with '27,280 transformer tokens (patch positions)' or '27,280 patch tokens', consistent with the geometry paragraph.
acceptance_test: The phrase 'latent tokens' does not appear where the post-patch count is meant; 'latent' is used only for the 109,120-cell grid.

page_hint: Appendix A §7A, 'Deriving attention FLOPs for a whole-clip video workload', opening paragraph
quoted_clause: This example applies the §1 principle (fewer sequential evaluations ≠ less total work) to a whole-clip denoiser
observed: Ambiguous cross-reference. Within §7A, '§1' is 'From corruption to learned generation', which does not contain the stated principle. The intended target is almost certainly Ch 3 §1 (the appendix's opening line of §7A says the section is 'The paper-by-paper treatment behind Ch 3 §1's alternative-inference scope note'), but the text as written points at a local section that does not contain the principle.
evidence: §7A's subsection list in this chunk: §1 is 'From corruption to learned generation'; the principle 'fewer sequential evaluations ≠ less total work' is not stated there.
root_cause: A cross-reference written for the Ch 3 context was carried into the appendix without qualifying the chapter.
correction: Write 'the Ch 3 §1 principle' (or name the principle and cite Ch 3 §1 explicitly).
acceptance_test: Every '§1' reference in §7A names a section that actually contains the referenced principle.

page_hint: Appendix A §1, 'What this means for the architect'
quoted_clause: DeepSeek shows the *constant factor itself* can be cut ~10–14× across the V4 variants (the ~14× end is V4-Flash's ~7%-of-V3.2 single-token KV, A.7)
observed: The band '~10–14×' is correct for the KV ratios (V4-Pro ~10% of V3.2 → 10×; V4-Flash ~7% → 1/0.07 ≈ 14.3×) but the preceding sentence in the same paragraph also reports FLOPs ratios of ~27% (Pro) and ~10% (Flash), i.e. 3.7× and 10×. 'The constant factor itself' is not specified as the KV constant, so a reader can reasonably read the band as covering both quantities, in which case the lower bound should be ~3.7×, not ~10×. The parenthetical disambiguates only the upper end.
evidence: Both sentences are in this chunk; 1/0.27 ≈ 3.7, 1/0.10 = 10, 1/0.07 ≈ 14.3.
root_cause: The band was computed for one metric while the sentence sits in a paragraph that introduces two metrics.
correction: Name the metric in the band: 'the KV constant itself can be cut ~10–14× across the V4 variants', and, if the FLOPs band is wanted, state it separately as '~3.7–10× on single-token inference FLOPs'.
acceptance_test: Every reduction band in §1 and §5 names the metric it applies to; a reader cannot apply the '~10–14×' band to the FLOPs figures.
